newsitem.title: UK: Next chief says "noone headhunting me".
newsitem.headline: Next chief says "noone headhunting me".

text.p: David Jones, chief executive of British fashion retailer Next Plc, rejected press reports on Monday as nonsense, saying he had not been approached by headhunters to take over the top job at Sears.
"I'm very happy in my current job. I am not intending to leave Next. As far as I am concerned no one is headhunting me for any job," said Jones in an interview from his carphone.
The Sunday Telegraph newspaper reported that Jones was offered the job of chief executive of retailer Sears but had decided to turn it down.

Many Sears shareholders are disgruntled with the dismal performance of the group and are calling for a radical shake-up including a demerger of its very profitable Selfridges department store and the sale of the struggling British Shoe Corporation.
Some investors also want to see Liam Strong, current chief executive of Sears bought in in 1992 to transform the retailer, replaced.

Jones is accredited with rescuing Next from the brink of collapse in the early 1990's -- in the midst of Britain's deepest recession since the second world war -- by combining a sell off programme of non-core assets, like mail order business Grattan, and a sharper focus on the core brand.
He sold shops and merged others, improving the brand's profile on the high street and reducing shoppers confusion about the range and type of products on sale.
On December 6 1990 Next shares reached a low of 7p compared with 573p today. In the full year to January 31, 1992 the company reported pretax profits of 12.3 million, last year it made 142 million.
Next now has a return on equity of 32.49 percent, against 12.5 percent at Burton Group, 11.79 percent at Laura Ashley, and 9.54 percent at Sears.
